sources.title: Mamata Tripathy, Folk Art at the Crossroads of Tradition and Modernity: A Study of Patta Painting in Orissa, JASO29/3(1998),197–211
sources.status: Original full article inspected; web403 but directdownload succeeded

findings.claim: Raghurajpur study based on observation, interviews, group discussions and case studies; identifies other centres including Sonepur, Parlakhemundi and Cuttack. Fieldwork dates not specified.

Biswakarma descent explicitly mythological. Author attributes royal settlement/tax-free-land account to temple chronicle; neither chronicle nor grant independently inspected. Do not present as proven founder/date.

Collective gathering of materials and shared transport/marketing described. Three service badas named for Jagannath, Balabhadra/Badathakura and Subhadra, with respective painting duties. Scope as study account, not exhaustive current temple-service registry.

Household craft with contributions from men and women; women preparing glue/chalk and polishing canvas, men layering cloth as described then. Skills transmitted in family work, not innate hereditary ability.

Workshops/training and exhibitions/cooperatives changed learning/marketing. Other communities also painting in Raghurajpur. Traditional material preparation retained for anasara paintings despite new commercial materials.

limits: Do not reproduce hierarchy, lowstatus or groupenterprising stereotypes.
Ritual calendar contains unsafe statements, e.g.RathYatra newmoon/Bamana tenth incarnation/Krishna birthday twelfthday; exclude exactcalendar and templeimage repainting claims absent verification.
No evidence all OdishanChitrakaras follow same duties/marriage/customs now.
Conclusion frames modernization as quality decline; do not adopt blanket moral judgment.
Entirearticle200wordbudget including notes, not separate budgets for eachsection.

findings: Table explicitly lists artist households in Raghurajpur:32Chitrakara,61Khandayat,10Bania,3Carpenter,2Nahaka,1Other. Do not misread concatenated last1 + printed37 as Other137. Table is Raghurajpur, not entire two-villagecluster or Odisha.
Authors describe three-to-four-year apprenticeships for boys and girls in gurukuls across Raghurajpur/Dandasahi; dated2008report, no currentenrolmentclaim.
Authors contrast market access and development support in Raghurajpur with Dandasahi, whose artisans faced extended credit/distressselling. Regionaldifference not innatecommunitytraits.
Artisan tiers link incomes to sketching/finishing/market access and supportwork; no need quote obsoleteincomevalues.
Report explicitly says difficult to attribute success to any single intervention/cause-effect relation. Lists exhibitions, training, marketing and heritagevillage initiatives.
limits: Reject Khandayat enterprising stereotype and broad legalstatus label.
Do not treat artisthouseholdcounts as totalcommunitypopulation.
Do not repeat unsupported royaltysettlement as provenformation.
No claim programmes or incomelevels persist2026.
